description: Answers "were there solar flares today?", "was there an X-class flare?", "is the Sun active?". The GOES X-ray level now (and whether it is current), the strongest X-ray flux of the last 24, 72 or 168 hours with its NOAA radio blackout level, and the solar flares NOAA recorded in that time: class, begin, peak and end, and whether one is in progress. Times in the asker's time zone. Data from NOAA SWPC.

hours.description: How far back to look: 24, 72 or 168 hours. Defaults to 24.

timeZone.description: IANA time zone of the person asking, such as Europe/Moscow or America/New_York. Local times and days use it. Defaults to UTC.

name: get_solar_flares

flares.description: Flares that began in the period, newest first.

endUnknown.description: No end recorded, but too long ago to call it in progress.

inProgress.description: No end recorded and begun less than 6 hours ago.

radioBlackout.description: NOAA radio blackout level of the peak: M1 is R1, M5 R2, X1 R3, X10 R4, X20 R5; null below M1.

flaresTruncated.description: True when only the 100 most recent flares are listed and older ones in the period are left out.

radioBlackout.description: NOAA radio blackout level of the peak: M1 is R1, M5 R2, X1 R3, X10 R4, X20 R5; null below M1.

peak.description: The highest X-ray flux of the period; at is the start of its 5-minute bucket for 24 hours, its hour for longer periods.

sources.description: Where the data comes from and on what terms.

asOf.description: When the latest measurement is no longer current: its local time.

class.description: GOES X-ray class of the latest measurement, 0.1-0.8 nm band, such as C1.2.

isCurrent.description: True until 30 minutes after the latest five-minute measurement ends.

title: Solar flares and X-rays
